title: When the Oath Sings
premise: Beatrix Yarrow has spent seven years hiding her forbidden gift of swordspeech—the magic that lets a blade remember its wielder's oaths—since the crown purged her order. When a dying courier gives her a map to the Hollow Vault, she learns the king of Thornfell is bound to an ancient parasite called the Regent, which feeds on oaths and grows stronger with every vow sworn in its king's name. Guided by a disgraced royal knight, Ser Aldric Vane, and hunted by the Regent's oath-sworn hunters, Beatrix must reach the vault where the first oath was forged and unbind it. In the end, Beatrix discovers only a freely broken oath can sever the Regent's power: she must publicly renounce the very vow that made her a swordspeaker, sacrificing her gift—and nearly her life—to free the king, then walk away from a kingdom that offers her everything except the invisibility she once wanted.
about_author: Astrid Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath rituals before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about the weight of promises, drawing on folklore of the mountain borderlands where she grew up.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Beatrix Yarrow guides contraband through the Thornfell passes, hiding her swordspeech behind silence and cheap steel. A checkpoint ambush forces her to draw her blade, and it whispers her old oath aloud—witnessed by no one she trusts. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of a woman shrinking her own life to survive.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: A bleeding courier collapses in Beatrix's barn, pressing a wax-sealed map into her hands and gasping that 'the crown eats him.' He dies before dawn; hunters arrive asking questions. Beatrix burns nothing and keeps the map. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: fear curdling into reluctant responsibility—the moment hiding stops being possible.

chapters.title: What the Blade Remembers
chapters.summary: Beatrix interrogates her own sword's memory for clues about the map's seal and relives the purge of her order seven years ago. Flashbacks reveal her mentor's last command: never speak for a crown again. POV: Beatrix, with memory interludes. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing, and the first hint that her gift is a key, not just a curse.

chapters.title: The Knight Without a Vow
chapters.summary: Ser Aldric Vane, stripped of his knighthood for doubting the king, intercepts Beatrix on the low road—not to arrest her, but to beg passage to the capital. He reveals rumors that the king speaks in two voices. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people who each broke something sacred.

chapters.title: Hunters Sworn
chapters.summary: The Regent's oath-sworn hunters attack a river ferry. Beatrix kills for the first time since the purge, and her blade screams with every death, broadcasting her location. She and Aldric flee into the deep fells. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: horror at what survival costs, and the theme's first hard price.

chapters.title: The City That Kneels
chapters.summary: Posing as a merchant's guard, Beatrix enters the capital and sees a city drowning in compulsory loyalty oaths—sworn daily, enforced by silver-collared clerks. The palace radiates wrongness her sword can feel. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: dread and recognition; the corruption of power made visible in ritual.

chapters.title: Two Voices in One Throat
chapters.summary: At a court feast, Beatrix witnesses King Edric address his lords—and hears the second voice beneath his words, ancient and hungry. Aldric confirms the king he served died slowly over three years. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: heartbreak disguised as duty; love for a liege curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Regent Explained
chapters.summary: In a burned library, an exiled scholar explains the Regent: a parasite born from the first oath ever sworn, sustained by every vow taken in the king's name. It cannot be killed—only unbound at the Hollow Vault where it was made. POV: Scholar, framed by Beatrix. Emotional beat: the scale of the problem becomes terrifyingly clear.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: To leave the capital alive, Beatrix bargains with a smuggler queen who demands a favor owed in blood. Aldric objects; Beatrix accepts anyway, hiding the terms. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice as habit, and the growing rift between pragmatism and trust.

chapters.title: Ambush at Greywater Bridge
chapters.summary: The hunters corner them at a bridge; Aldric takes a wound meant for Beatrix and confesses, half-delirious, that he reported her order's location years ago under duress. She saves him anyway. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: guilt confessed, forgiveness withheld but not refused—love against duty taking root.

chapters.title: The Map's True Road
chapters.summary: Deciphering the courier's marginalia, Beatrix realizes the map leads through the Underfell—a living labyrinth where oaths spoken aloud become binding law. They must travel in total silence for three days. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension; intimacy built without words.

chapters.title: Silence in the Underfell
chapters.summary: In the lightless passages, a hunter infiltrates the party disguised by stolen vows. Beatrix unmasks them only when her sword refuses to sing for the impostor's lies. Blood is spilled; the debt to the smuggler queen comes due early. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: paranoia, then fierce clarity about who she chooses to trust.

chapters.title: The Queen's Due
chapters.summary: The smuggler queen collects: she wants Beatrix's swordspeech used to forge an unbreakable contract making the fells independent forever. Beatrix refuses, forfeiting protection, and the alliance shatters. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the cost of integrity; power offered and declined.

chapters.title: What Aldric Saw
chapters.summary: Aldric recounts the night he knelt before the Regent wearing the king's face and swore a second, secret oath—one that now lets the Regent track him anywhere. He decides to leave the group as bait. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: shame transformed into resolve; love expressed as departure.

chapters.title: The Hollow Vault Found
chapters.summary: Beatrix reaches the Vault alone: a cathedral of black stone where the first oath hangs in the air like a held breath. Inside, she finds not a weapon but a witness-stone recording every oath ever sworn to the crown—including her own. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: awe and vertigo before the machinery of power itself.

chapters.title: The Regent's Bargain
chapters.summary: The Regent arrives wearing the king's body and offers Beatrix restoration of her order, her name cleared, her gift legitimized—if she will swear herself to the crown and become its new Voice. It shows her the purge, her mentor's grave, everything she lost. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: temptation at its most personal; power's corruption whispering in her own accent.

chapters.title: Aldric's Last Oath
chapters.summary: Aldric, delivered as bait, breaks his secret oath aloud before the Vault—knowing the breaking will kill him—to buy Beatrix one unguarded hour. Dying, he tells her the truth she needs: the Regent cannot survive a freely broken founding oath. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the purest form of love against duty.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Beatrix draws her sword and speaks her original oath into the witness-stone—then renounces it, freely and completely, unmaking the pattern the Regent feeds on. The Vault convulses; the parasite tears loose from the king across a hundred miles. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: climax—grief, liberation, and the terrible cost as her gift gutters out with the oath.

chapters.title: The King Waking
chapters.summary: King Edric wakes in his own body after three years, remembering everything the Regent did with his hands. He summons Beatrix to offer her a marshal's rank, her order refounded, everything she lost restored. POV: Edric. Emotional beat: hollow victory; a crown learning what it cost.

chapters.title: Everything Except Silence
chapters.summary: Beatrix refuses the king's gifts. Her swordspeech is gone—or so she believes until her old blade hums faintly at her hip, changed but not dead. She asks instead for one thing: the road out of Thornfell, unwitnessed. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: quiet defiance; redefining survival as freedom rather than safety.

chapters.title: The Road Unwritten
chapters.summary: Beatrix buries Aldric beneath a rowan tree and walks the smuggler roads south, carrying the courier's map as a keepsake. Rumors follow her of a nameless guide who never swears oaths. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: mourning braided with hope; the person she chose to become.

chapters.title: When the Oath Sings
chapters.summary: Epilogue: in the rebuilt Vault, the witness-stone holds a new entry—an unnamed woman's freely broken vow, sung back by the stone whenever young knights are taught what oaths cost. Far away on a mountain pass, Beatrix's sword sings softly in the wind, and she lets it. POV: omniscient coda. Emotional beat: resonance and release—the price paid becomes a lesson kept.
